transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-12
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~51 minutes
Attendees: Anna (Redwood AE), Jamal (Redwood SE), Karen (CTO - SpruceFold), Liu (NetOps), Marta (Security), Omar (Cloud Eng)

Summary:
Quick intake to validate SpruceFold's network posture and constraints for a Private/VPC deployment of Redwood. Main topics: VPC peering vs PrivateLink, Transit Gateway topology, egress/region restrictions, KMS and key management, SOC2/audit logging. Agreement to run a focused network design session and share diagrams + security pack.

Topics:
- VPC peering and Transit GW
- Private endpoints / PrivateLink alternatives
- CIDR/IP range planning and overlap concerns
- Regional availability and data residency (APAC restrictions)
- Egress bandwidth and NAT/egress firewall requirements
- KMS/HSM integration, audit logs, SSO

Action items (short):
- Redwood to share peering checklist + sample route tables
- Customer to send CIDR ranges and list of regions with constraints
- SE deep-dive scheduled 2027-11-19

Transcript body:
[00:00] Anna: Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. Quick intros, i'm Anna with Redwood, and Jamal's our systems engineer.
[00:10] Karen: Hi. Karen here, CTO at SpruceFold. We have Liu on netops, Marta on security, Omar's on cloud eng. Thanks for making time.
[00:18] Jamal: Great, thanks. The goal is to understand your current network layout and any blockers for a private deployment, any compliance/regional gating, and then propose an approach.
[00:28] Liu: Sounds good. We run a multi-account AWS setup, transit gw in us-east-1 and eu-west-1. APAC is limited because of data residency rules, we cannot exit singapore region for customer data.
[00:40] Marta: And from security — we need all audit logs to go to our SIEM, KMS keys are customer-managed. SOC2 is in flight but we need to understand Redwood's retention and network audit capabilities.
[00:52] Anna: Sure. Quick note: Redwood Private supports VPC peering, Transit Gateway attachments, and PrivateLink-style private endpoints depending on customer preference. There are tradeoffs with each — we'll walk through them.
[01:05] Karen: Can you clarify the difference in practice? We heard from another vendor that private endpoints are better for cross-account access.
[01:14] Jamal: Right — so peering is direct route-based connectivity but doesn't scale well for many accounts and has limitations on transitive routing. Transit GW centralizes routing and is usually our recommendation for large orgs. PrivateLink (private endpoints) presents a network interface in your VPC to the service — it is great for strict egress control and is often used when peering or transit isn't allowed.
[01:36] Liu: Do you support multiple attachments to the transit gw across regions? We saw notes about us-east-1 and eu-west-1.
[01:45] Jamal: Yes, we can attach regional deployments, but we typically recommend colocating the Redwood private control plane in the region where the data must stay. For APAC constraints we can provision a regional control plane in ap-southeast-1.
[01:59] Marta: That was my question — can we keep all inference traffic within ap-southeast-1 for APAC customers?
[02:06] Anna: Yes, you can pin model serving to a region. There are a couple options: Hosted in Redwood's region (we'd set up a private deployment there) or Dedicated reserved capacity in your VPC. In both cases you can enforce region restriction policies.
[02:20] Karen: On the topic of keys — we use AWS KMS with a customer-managed CMK. Do you support HSM or CMK integration?
[02:28] Jamal: We support KMS integrations; for Private we can integrate with your KMS via IAM roles and key policies. HSM is possible but tends to be a more bespoke setup. We'll share our KMS integration doc.
[02:38] Omar: Egress — what does your typical egress look like? We want to know whether we need NAT gateways or if you recommend direct peering for egress to the service.
[02:48] Anna: For private endpoint deployments, traffic is internal — usually you won't need additional NAT for model traffic. For monitoring/metrics and outbound updates we may need controlled egress to Redwood control plane endpoints, which we can minimize with private interconnects.
[03:04] Liu: Any special port requirements or protocols? We are strict about only opening a couple ports, and everything goes through our FW.
[03:11] Jamal: Primarily HTTPS (443) for control-plane, and gRPC for data plane if you use some advanced SDKs; but typically 443 covers it. We'll provide a port list.
[03:22] Karen: How do you handle IP ranges? We have a bunch of subnets and overlapping CIDRs can be a blocker.
[03:29] Jamal: Overlap is common — we usually do either NAT-based routing or we recommend re-IPing shared spaces. For Transit GW you can use route table mapping to avoid conflicts, but it's messier. Best if you can provide the CIDR ranges up front.
[03:45] Marta: Audit logs — we need to centralize logs in our SIEM and have immutable retention. Is Redwood able to export token-level logs and request traces?
[03:55] Anna: Yes, Redwood Console provides per-token cost and latency breakdowns, plus request traces. For Private we can configure log forwarding into your logging cluster — S3/CloudWatch/Splunk depending on your stack.
[04:10] Karen: Good. What about SSO / SAML for admin access?
[04:15] Anna: Supported. We have SSO options including SAML/Okta, and RBAC for tenant-level roles. For Private we can connect to your IdP via metadata file.
[04:25] Liu: One of our compliance constraints is zone isolation — certain teams are in a restricted spine. Can Redwood be deployed in a way that enforces subaccount-level isolation?
[04:34] Jamal: Yes. We recommend separate VPCs for isolated workloads with Transit GW attachments or separate private endpoints. That way you get isolation at the network border.
[04:45] Omar: Performance — latency is critical for one of our customer-facing features. How do you measure and guarantee latency?
[04:53] Jamal: We publish performance profiles per model and can run a pre-prod perf benchmark from your environment. The Dedicated pools give you predictable throughput. We'll plan a benchmark during the pilot.
[05:06] Karen: Are there any limits on concurrent connections or token throughput we should be aware of?
[05:12] Jamal: Limits depend on the deployment tier. Hosted has shared limits, Dedicated has guaranteed concurrency. We'll include suggested concurrency numbers and a recommended instance sizing for your workloads.
[05:24] Marta: For SOC2 evidence, we need network diagrams and proof of encryption in transit and at rest.
[05:31] Anna: We'll include the network security packet and our SOC2 summary. For Private deployments we can provide diagrams that show the routing patterns and how logs are exported.
[05:40] Liu: Region gating — some of our EU customers can't have data leave the EU for any reason. How quickly can you provision a regional instance?
[05:48] Jamal: Provisioning time depends on capacity; typically a regional private control plane can be standing in days to a week if we have capacity and the proc is clear. For reserved Dedicated capacity we'd coordinate timelines during contracting.
[06:01] Karen: What about cost tradeoffs between Transit GW + peering vs PrivateLink? We need an estimate to present to finance.
[06:10] Anna: PrivateLink often costs more per endpoint but simplifies security and avoids route table complexity. Transit GW scales well but there is TGW hourly cost plus data processing. We'll send a simple TCO snapshot comparing both.
[06:25] Omar: On the peering side — are there cross-account helpers you provide? Some vendors give CloudFormation templates.
[06:31] Jamal: We do have CF/Terraform templates for peering, route tables, and sample TGW attachments — we'll attach those.
[06:40] Marta: Encryption keys again — can you show how key rotation is handled? We have strict rotation policies.
[06:46] Jamal: We can tie into your KMS rotation; Redwood's runtime can use CMKs with IAM role-based access and honor rotation. We'll include rotation steps in the KMS doc.
[06:58] Anna: Quick check — any hard stop items blocking a pilot?
[07:02] Karen: Two: CIDR overlap possibility, and APAC regional isolation. If both are resolvable, we're good to pilot.
[07:12] Liu: Also, we need to understand the egress audit — how will you show that data never leaves the region?
[07:19] Jamal: We can produce trace logs on a per-request basis and show route hops; for additional assurance we can run a small traceroute/latency test from within your VPC to the private endpoints during the pilot.
[07:30] Omar: Any special firewall devices we need to be aware of? We use Palo Alto and F5 LB in front of our apps.
[07:37] Anna: Not typically. For PrivateLink you'll point to an endpoint service; for peering/TGW it's route-based. We'll share the firewall rule set.
[07:46] Karen: About DNS — do you require private hosted zones?
[07:50] Jamal: Yes, for PrivateLink we recommend private hosted zones to resolve the service hostnames internally. For peering/TGW we sometimes use host entries or shared resolver endpoints. We have docs for both.
[08:02] Marta: Do you keep request payloads in logs by default? We have PII constraints, want only metadata.
[08:08] Anna: By default logs are metadata only; payload capture is opt-in for debugging and subject to strict controls. We'll document the default retention and redaction behavior.
[08:18] Karen: Can we get a short architecture sketch now just high-level?
[08:22] Jamal: Sure — imagine your accounts with VPCs attached to a Transit GW in each region, Redwood private endpoints or TGW attachments in the same region; route tables configured so data flows stay local, logs forwarded to your SIEM, KMS for encryption.
[08:39] Liu: When you said "Private endpoints" — is that the AWS "Interface VPC Endpoint" PrivateLink?
[08:45] Jamal: Yes exactly — interface endpoints. Sometimes docs call them PrivateLink or Private Endpoint interchangeably.
[08:52] Karen: Any regulatory concerns around storing model artifacts? We have to know where model cache or KV cache resides.
[08:59] Jamal: Model cache (KV cache) in our Private deployment runs in the customer's VPC or in the same regional deployment; we can ensure it is region-bound. There might be ephemeral SSD-backed caches on nodes but nothing leaves the region unless configured.
[09:15] Marta: Do you support VPC endpoints for S3/CloudWatch to avoid public egress for logs?
[09:21] Jamal: Yes — we recommend S3 gateway endpoints or interface endpoints depending on your config. We'll provide the recommended setup.
[09:29] Anna: Ok, quick pause — i'm going to note the main deliverables: peering checklist, CF/Terraform templates, SOC2 + network security pack, sample TGW configs, and timeline for pilot provisioning. Anything missing?
[09:43] Karen: A sample benchmark plan for latency tests would be helpful.
[09:47] Jamal: We'll include that in the templates and propose test cases focusing on p95 latency and tail latencies.
[09:55] Liu: We also need to know about burst capacity — can you handle sudden spikes?
[09:59] Jamal: Dedicated capacity supports predictable bursts; for Private we can configure autoscaling policies and reserved capacity. For strict SLAs we recommend Dedicated.
[10:09] Omar: Regarding firewall egress — do you need us to open any ephemeral port ranges for node-to-node communication?
[10:15] Jamal: Usually only for cluster control-plane; we'll list the ephemeral ranges if needed, but in many setups it's tunneled over 443.
[10:25] Marta: Data residency again — for APAC we probably require on-prem. Is on-prem private deployment supported?
[10:33] Anna: Yes, Redwood Private has an on-prem package for regulated workloads, but that is more involved — includes an air-gapped install and additional compliance checks. We'll flag that as a potential path if regional cloud provisioning isn't acceptable.
[10:47] Karen: Can you summarize the security model for Private quickly?
[10:50] Jamal: Sure — customer VPC contains the serving nodes, keys are customer-managed, logs forwarded to your SIEM, SSO for admin access, RBAC for tenant segmentation, and network isolation via VPC/TGW/PrivateLink.
[11:03] Liu: Is there a minimum contract or commitment to get a dedicated regional deployment?
[11:09] Anna: For Dedicated capacity there is usually a monthly or annual commitment. For Private self-hosted we can do a one-time setup plus ongoing support fees. We'll include slides on pricing options.
[11:21] Karen: On network provider side — do you have any preferred partners for cross-connects or direct links?
[11:27] Jamal: We work with common cloud partners and can co-ordinate cross-connects; if you have an existing partner we can plug into that.
[11:34] Omar: For the pilot, what are the success criteria we should define?
[11:38] Anna: Typical success criteria: p95 latency under X ms for specific prompts, stable concurrency for N users, logs forwarded reliably to SIEM, and proof that data never leaves region. We can tailor those numbers in writing.
[11:53] Marta: We will provide the security and compliance checklist to match those success criteria.
[11:58] Jamal: Great — venn plan: we'll prepare a network design session, send templates + security docs, and provision a test tenant.
[12:07] Karen: Timeline — we'd like the deep-dive next week if possible.
[12:11] Anna: Jamal is available on 2027-11-19 for the SE-led design session. We'll schedule now.
[12:18] Liu: Small thing — do you support private DNS resolvers across accounts?
[12:23] Jamal: Yes, Route 53 Resolver endpoints or forwarding rules depending on your approach.
[12:30] Omar: Anything on monotoring or trace sampling? We need to make sure trace IDs propagate into our trace collection.
[12:37] Jamal: We emit traces and can include trace IDs in logs to correlate. Sampling rates can be configured.
[12:45] Marta: For legal, we might need a data protection addendum; can you surface the DPA?
[12:51] Anna: We'll include the DPA and standard data processing terms.
[12:57] Karen: On the topic of model updates — if you push a model patch, will that cause a rolling restart? How do we control maintenance windows?
[13:06] Jamal: There are rollout policies — canary and A/B and you can schedule maintenance windows. For Private we agree on maintenance windows with you.
[13:18] Liu: So next steps — we'll gather the CIDRs and send them to Anna, and you'll share the templates and security docs.
[13:25] Anna: Yep. I'll follow up with the checklist and schedule.
[13:30] Omar: One more, about telemetry retention — how long do you keep request traces?
[13:36] Anna: Default retention is 30 days for traces, longer for logs if needed; for Private we can adjust per contract.
[13:44] Marta: Ok that sounds reasonable.
[13:47] Jamal: Any blockers from your side for the pilot timing?
[13:51] Karen: No, we'll aim to have the CIDR list by 11/15.
[13:56] Anna: Great — to wrap up, we'll send: network peering checklist, TGW sample configs, CF/Terraform templates, security and SOC2 docs, KMS integration docs, and a proposed pilot plan with benchmarks.
[14:12] Karen: Thanks everyone. Look forward to the design session next week.
[14:16] Anna: Thanks all — meeting adjourned.

[End of recording]

Notes on transcript: occasional mis-heard words (e.g., "key vee cache" for KV cache), some speaker attribution could be approximate due to overlapping talk.
